result.title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop ML4Molecules: Agentic Systems for Molecular Sciences
result.summary: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. A difficult case arises when both genes in a test pair were seen individually during training, but their combination was not. In this setting, standard OOD methods often fail because neither gene appears unfamiliar on its own. We therefore compare each model prediction with a simple additive prediction obtained by summing the two observed single-gene effects. The difference between them, which we call additive disagreement (AD), measures how much extra interaction effect the model introduces for an unseen combination. Across eight prediction methods and three Perturb-seq datasets, specialised neural predictors do not consistently outperform this simple additive baseline. More importantly, predictions with larger deviations from the additive baseline tend to have larger errors. Conventional output-based and embedding-based confidence signals are inconsistent across datasets and models, whereas AD remains informative across all evaluated compositional settings. We further study how this signal can guide decisions in an agentic perturbation-screening workflow. The code is available at https://github.com/zygao930/OOD.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究基因组合扰动效应的外推预测：提出「加性分歧」（AD），即模型预测与两个已观测单基因效应之和的差值，用以衡量模型对未见组合额外引入的互作效应，并在八个预测方法与三个 Perturb-seq 数据集上比较其与传统输出／嵌入置信信号的表现，以及在 agentic 筛选流程中的决策作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 来自基因组扰动筛选这一较远领域，但「偏离简单加性基线的程度越大则误差越大」这一结构化可靠性信号，可能为 latent 推理中的组合泛化诊断、置信估计与「继续取证据／停止」的决策提供类比线索，可供核查。
